title: Guide - Calming an Anxious Heart - Cast your cares

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Calming an Anxious Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Cast Your Cares. <short pause> You may have been carrying something for days, or for years. <short pause> Let's take a few minutes to share the weight of it.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Settle into a position that asks very little of you. <short pause> Let your arms be heavy. <short pause> Turn your hands so the palms can rest. <short pause> Breathe in, just as much as you need... <short pause> and breathe out, as if you were lowering something carefully to the ground.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Have you ever carried heavy bags a long way, and refused every offer of help? <short pause> After a while, your fingers curl around the handles. <short pause> Even when you reach the door, it takes a moment to open them. <short pause> We can carry worry like that for so long... <short pause> that holding on begins to feel like the safe thing.

David carried a worry that had a face. <short pause> In Psalm fifty-five, he has been hurt by a close friend, and he says he wishes he had wings like a dove, so he could fly away. <short pause> He can't fly away. <short pause> But he finds something else he can do. <short pause> He tells us in verse twenty-two.
Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He shall sustain thee. <short pause> Notice that God takes hold of more than the burden. <short pause> He takes hold of you. <short pause> Even if the trouble is still here tomorrow, you will not be standing under it alone.

So what have you been holding? <short pause> Perhaps a person you can't change. <short pause> A decision you can't see the end of. <short pause> Money, or health, or a child you love. <short pause> Choose one burden for now, just one, and let it come to mind.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Picture it as something in your hands. <short pause> It might be a stone, or a box, or a bag with a worn strap. <short pause> Feel how much it weighs. <short pause> You can be honest about that. <short pause> Lord, this is heavy. <short pause> I have been holding it for a long time.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now imagine His hands beneath yours. <short pause> You don't have to throw it, or be sure, or be strong. <short pause> Just lower it a little, until He has some of the weight. <short pause> Breathe out... <short pause> and lower it a little more. <short pause> Breathe out... <short pause> and loosen one finger. <short pause> Then another.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And when you are ready, let your hands open. <short pause> Lord, I give You the outcome. <short pause> I give You what other people choose. <short pause> I give You tomorrow. <short pause> I keep only the next small, loving thing that is mine to do.

You may pick it up again in an hour. <short pause> Most of us do. <short pause> That isn't failure. <short pause> It only means you can hand it back again, as many times as you need to. <short pause> He will not grow tired of receiving it. <short pause> And sometimes He sustains us through other hands... a friend, a pastor, a doctor, a counselor. <short pause> You can let them help as well.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Listen again, with empty hands. <short pause> Cast thy burden upon the Lord... <short pause> and he shall sustain thee. <short pause> Sustain. <short pause> To hold up. <short pause> To keep going. <short pause> That is what He is doing for you, even now.

Let's pray. <short pause> Faithful God, <short pause> I hand You the burden I have pictured here. <short pause> Care for it better than I can. <short pause> Hold me up where I am worn thin, and keep my heart from being swept away. <short pause> When I reach for the weight again, gently remind me whose it is. <short pause> Amen.
Before you go, open and close your hands once, slowly. <short pause> Let them remember how it feels to be open. <short pause> They are free now, for the next small thing. <short pause> Go lightly.
